en: A lynx of the high pass in its slate-grey winter coat, ear tufts white with frost. It takes the slowest of a line, the way it takes the last of a flock.
A pale moth whose larvae live in old keth cords. The knots it ate come out on its wings, and the Ullari say a few of them can still be read.
A mountain tortoise whose shell is frost-split scree. It sleeps through the summers and the passes are cleared around it.

A woolback grown past any herd's size, its fleece felted into plates that hang to its knees. A red herd-cord still runs through the wool: somebody once named it and walked it home every night. It drinks at the weeping wall above Quellan, and the snow comes down when it is angry.
Something is bringing the snow down on the road. Climb on.
Find the Saint of the weaving-hall.
Spend the night at Quellan's inn.
Down the other side, toward Ansedra. Don't look back.
A herder's boy needs a knot tied on the pass.
The red herd-cord belongs to someone in Quellan.
Cord moths unpick the wards you've woven. Strike them before your wards are gone.
Every charge brings more snow down. The field shows what the next one costs.
A pad of felted woolback fleece, dense enough to turn a blade. Used in Customize.
Salted Ullari tea, thick with butter. The highlands say it puts the breath back into you.
A bangle of knotted Ullari cord. A keth-reader tied it and wouldn't say what it reads.
A highland shield faced with woolback felt. It takes a blow quietly.
